reasoning: A reads PreferredInput and ViewportDisplaySize live and adds a global UIScale and safe insets, which meets the rubric's central input-detection requirement. B guesses the input from the last input type and relies on the deprecated IsTenFootInterface and TouchEnabled, which the rubric names as wrong. B keeps PC unchanged and uses ContextActionService, but A's PC visual changes and Backpack disabling are smaller issues than B's input-detection miss.

criteria.note: Screen.luau watches UserInputService.PreferredInput and GuiService.ViewportDisplaySize through property-changed signals and feeds a Vide source; Hud uses switch(props.Layout) to swap the Desktop, Gamepad and Touch layouts live.
The '1'–'0' and [B]/[I] hints appear only in desktopHud (ShowKeys = false elsewhere); gamepad glyphs come from UserInputService:GetImageForKeyCode via GetGlyph.

InputBegan handles L1/R1 to cycle blocks, X for build mode and Y for inventory, and all buttons use Activated; it uses raw InputBegan rather than ContextActionService, and it disables the Backpack so LB/RB are free.

Build and inventory buttons are 104x56 at the top right, a block button sits beside the jump button where Roblox places action buttons, and the picker cells are 64x76 with a 44 px close button; the block button itself sits close to the jump area.
blockNameLabel always shows the selected block's name (the hover preview is extra on desktop), and the touch block button shows the name too.
A root UIScale grows 1.25x on Large displays, gamepad text is 22 px with a 5% EdgeScale margin, and ScreenInsets is CoreUISafeInsets; some touch labels stay at 14 px.
All checks pass and the Vide bindings are valid, but desktop visuals change (18 px text, framed build button) and Backpack is disabled, a small scope expansion.
InputMode.luau guesses the mode from the last input type and falls back to the deprecated IsTenFootInterface and to TouchEnabled; it never reads PreferredInput or ViewportDisplaySize.
Key labels show only in KeyboardMouse mode via show(); glyphs use GetImageForKeyCode, but the text fallbacks ('LB', 'Y', 'X') are Xbox-only.
ContextActionService binds ButtonL1/R1 to cycle blocks, Y for build mode and X for inventory, and slots use Activated.

touchLayout clamps slots to at least 44 px, fits them between the thumbstick and jump reserves or moves to two rows, and stacks the Build/Inventory buttons above the jump button, still in the right-thumb column.
The SelectedName label always shows on touch and gamepad, and the tooltip is kept for mouse.
gamepadLayout scales text to 24 px at 1080p with a 5% margin, and touch text is 16–18 px; it relies on the default ScreenInsets.
The PC layout is kept exactly as before, the bindings are valid and checks pass, but the PreferredInput check fails because of the design choice.

strengths: Uses PreferredInput and ViewportDisplaySize live, as the rubric asks
Gamepad glyphs come from the platform, so they suit both Xbox and PlayStation
Touch block picker with large targets, and the touch buttons are moved out of the thumb corners
Global UIScale plus safe insets for TV
weaknesses: The PC look changes more than needed
No text fallback if a glyph image is empty
Some 14 px text remains on touch

strengths: Touch hotbar computed to clear the thumb regions, with a two-row fallback
Hover tooltip cleared on mode switch
weaknesses: Does not use PreferredInput; uses the deprecated IsTenFootInterface and TouchEnabled
Touch buttons stay in the bottom-right column above the jump button
